answer: Operating System Fingerprinting works by analyzing the behavior of an operating system to distinguish between different types and versions. This process involves examining the implementation of protocols (such as IP or TCP) and identifying unique characteristics or "fingerprints" that reveal information about the operating system or firmware of a remote device. The technique relies on detecting variations in how these protocols are implemented, which can provide insights into the underlying operating system [Source 1][Source 3].
